title: Fathom Review 2026: What It Does Well, Where It Stops
summary: An honest Fathom review for 2026: what the free AI notetaker does well, where it reaches its limits, and the signs that a sales team has outgrown it.
body_markdown:
Fathom is probably the best free AI notetaker you can put on a sales call, and that sentence contains both the praise and the limit: what it produces is notes.


## 01


What does Fathom actually do?


Fathom is an AI notetaker. It joins your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams meetings as a bot participant, records and transcribes them, and delivers a summary with action items shortly after the call ends. You can clip highlights and share them. Paid team tiers add CRM sync, shared call libraries, and team-level controls.


Setup takes minutes, which is part of the appeal: connect your calendar, and the bot starts showing up.


## 02


What Fathom does well


- **The free tier is a real product.** Individuals get recording, transcription, and summaries without paying, and without the artificial ceilings that make most free tiers a demo. This is Fathom's defining move and the reason it spread.
- **Summaries arrive fast and read well.** The post-call summary lands while the call is still fresh, and it is usually accurate enough to paste into a CRM note unedited.
- **Low training burden.** Reps do not need to learn anything. The notes appear.
- **CRM sync earns its price.** On paid tiers, pushing summaries into the CRM removes a chunk of admin work that reps otherwise skip.


For a founder doing their own sales, or a small team whose main problem is remembering what was said, Fathom is an easy recommendation.


## 03


How much does Fathom cost?


The individual tier is free, and it is the version most people mean when they recommend Fathom. Paid team tiers add CRM sync, shared libraries, and admin controls, with per-seat pricing published on Fathom's site. Prices change, so check the current page rather than a review, including this one. The useful framing: individuals rarely need to pay, and teams pay for sync and control rather than better notes.


## 04


What is setup and day-to-day use like?


Setup is connecting your calendar and choosing which meetings the bot joins: external only, everything, or per-meeting. Day one is genuinely done in minutes.


The day-two details deserve a moment of thought. The bot appears in the meeting under a visible name, so decide what it is called and whether reps should mention it up front. Recording consent rules vary by region, and the safe pattern is an explicit sentence at the top of the call. None of this is hard; all of it is better decided by a manager once than improvised by each rep live.


## 05


Where Fathom stops


**Everything arrives after the call.** The summary is faithful, and it faithfully records the moment the deal stalled: the security question the rep could not answer, the competitor claim that went unchallenged. Notes describe the problem; they do not prevent it.


**There is a bot in the room.** Fathom attends as a visible participant. Some prospects do not care; some do, and some compliance teams mind on the prospect's side. If that friction matters to you, we have written about[assistants that work without a meeting bot](https://www.caretta.so/blog/ai-sales-assistant-without-meeting-bot) .


**Analytics are light.** Fathom is not trying to be Gong. There are no deep coaching workflows, tracker programmes, or deal-risk models. Managers who want to run a coaching motion on top of call data will hit the ceiling quickly.


**The knowledge stays in documents.** Summaries accumulate in a library. Nothing from call forty-nine automatically helps the rep on call fifty. The institutional memory exists, but it is passive.


## 06


When has a sales team outgrown Fathom?


The signs are consistent:


1. Reps face the same hard questions on every call, and the answers live in summaries nobody rereads.
2. Managers want coaching and deal signals, not just notes.
3. Someone is manually pasting summary fragments into onboarding docs.
4. "Let me get back to you" is a normal sentence on your calls.


The first three point to analytics platforms. The fourth points to a real-time assistant: software that listens to the live conversation and puts the relevant answer on the rep's screen while the prospect is still talking. That is the category Caretta is in, and the honest framing is that it solves a different problem from Fathom rather than a bigger version of the same one. Our[guide to AI tools for sales calls by category](https://www.caretta.so/blog/best-ai-tools-for-sales-calls) maps the landscape.


## 07


Fathom vs the alternatives


Against Otter, Fathom is more meeting-shaped and its summaries are more directly usable for sales, while Otter covers a wider range of transcription jobs. Against Granola, Fathom does more but brings a bot; Granola stays out of the room and does less. Against Gong-class platforms, there is no contest in either direction: different budgets, different jobs, and nobody cross-shops them for long.


If you are leaving, your data comes with you; we wrote a practical guide to[exporting your data from Otter and Fathom](https://www.caretta.so/blog/export-data-otter-fathom) .


## 08


Verdict


Fathom earns its reputation. It does the job it promises, the free tier is genuinely free, and nothing about it feels like a trap. Recommend it to any founder or small team drowning in unrecorded conversations.


Judge it for what it is, though: a memory, not a colleague. The moment your problem shifts from "we forget what was said" to "we lose deals in the conversation itself", you have left notetaker territory, and no notetaker upgrade will follow you there.
